title: The AASM Manual for the Scoring of Sleep and Associated Events, Version 3
sourceRole: current scoring, staging, respiratory, cardiac, movement, and technical terminology
authority: controlling scoring terminology for this study system
apaReference: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
copyrightBoundary: Glossary term names are inventoried. Learner definitions and memory clues are original Sleep Pathways Guild summaries rather than reproduced AASM glossary prose.

items.definition: A repeating pattern in which brief anterior tibialis EMG activity alternates between the two legs during sleep or arousals.
items.memoryClue: ALMA alternates legs.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Very slow EEG activity in the delta frequency range used when describing slow-wave activity.
items.memoryClue: Delta is the slowest major sleep EEG band.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: The voltage difference recorded between two electrodes or inputs, such as an EEG, EOG, or EMG channel.
items.memoryClue: A derivation is a difference between two inputs.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Chin EMG activity that clearly rises above the low baseline level used to judge muscle activity during sleep, regardless of how long the burst lasts.
items.memoryClue: Think amplitude above the quiet REM baseline.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Brief, small limb EMG bursts during sleep that may produce tiny visible movements or no obvious movement at all.
items.memoryClue: Fragmentary = tiny, brief muscle fragments.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A respiratory event with near-complete loss of airflow for the minimum duration required by the applicable AASM apnea rule.
items.memoryClue: Apnea means airflow nearly stops.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: The number of apneas plus hypopneas per hour of total sleep time.
items.memoryClue: AHI uses sleep time as the denominator.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A pause in cardiac rhythm long enough to meet the AASM scoring threshold for asystole.
items.memoryClue: Asystole is a prolonged cardiac pause.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: An irregularly irregular rhythm in which consistent P waves are replaced by rapid atrial activity.
items.memoryClue: Irregularly irregular with no consistent P waves.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Fast EEG activity in the beta frequency range.
items.memoryClue: Beta is fast EEG activity.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Vertical EOG deflections produced by blinking, typically seen during wakefulness.
items.memoryClue: Blinking is a wake clue.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A sinus rhythm that falls below the AASM sleep bradycardia rate threshold for the patient’s age group.
items.memoryClue: Use the sleep-specific rate threshold, not a wake-only rule.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Age measured from the mother’s last menstrual period to birth or to the time being described, used when evaluating infant sleep.
items.memoryClue: Gestational age starts before birth.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: An ECG rhythm in which pacemaker-generated impulses are visible and drive atrial, ventricular, or dual-chamber activation.
items.memoryClue: Look for pacing spikes before captured beats.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A high-amplitude slow EEG pattern seen in infants and used in infant sleep-stage description.
items.memoryClue: HVS = high voltage + slow activity.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A hypopnea that meets scoring criteria and shows features indicating reduced central respiratory drive rather than upper-airway obstruction.
items.memoryClue: Central = reduced drive without obstructive clues.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A brief rhythmic foot or leg EMG activity pattern that appears around sleep onset and is usually an incidental PSG finding.
items.memoryClue: Hypnagogic = around sleep onset.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A periodic breathing pattern with repeated waxing and waning ventilation separated by central apneas or hypopneas.
items.memoryClue: Crescendo-decrescendo breathing with central events.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A high-amplitude rhythmic EEG pattern of childhood that appears around sleep onset and can occur in N1 or N2 sleep.
items.memoryClue: A normal pediatric sleep-onset pattern, not automatically epileptiform.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.term: Chronological age (also known as postnatal or legal age)
items.definition: Age counted from the date of birth, distinct from gestational or postmenstrual age.
items.memoryClue: Chronological age starts at birth.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A graph showing the sequence of scored sleep stages across the recording.
items.memoryClue: Hypnogram = sleep stages over time.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A sensor system that measures pressure changes at the nose through a nasal cannula and provides a signal related to airflow.
items.memoryClue: Pressure changes are used as a surrogate for airflow.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A qualifying reduction in airflow that lasts long enough and is accompanied by the required oxygen desaturation and/or arousal under the applicable AASM rule.
items.memoryClue: Hypopnea = partial airflow reduction plus a qualifying consequence.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
